name: rgbds
why: A Game Boy assembler and linker toolchain, a real doorway into writing code for retro hardware.

brief.what_it_is: RGBDS (Rednex Game Boy Development System) is a free assembler and linker package for the Game Boy and Game Boy Color. It has four tools: RGBASM (assembler), RGBLINK (linker), RGBFIX (ROM checksum and header fixer), and RGBGFX (PNG-to-Game Boy graphics converter). Source assembly code and PNG art go in, and a playable ROM comes out. The homepage says each tool can be swapped for a custom one or used standalone in another process.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames it as giving developers complete control over the console with no middle-man, so debugging is simpler, and pushing the Game Boy's limited capabilities by writing native assembly. It also positions itself as a long-running open source project (dating back to 1997) that supports the homebrew community.
brief.how_it_works: Each stage of the pipeline is a separate program: RGBGFX converts images to Game Boy tile formats, RGBASM assembles source into object files, RGBLINK links those objects into a ROM, and RGBFIX patches the ROM header and checksum. The README and homepage do not describe the internal object format or language syntax in detail.

brief.install_notes: The homepage has an Install page with platform-specific instructions (rgbds.gbdev.io/install/), which I did not fetch. Building from source needs make or cmake. On Windows, any SUFFIX must include the .exe extension. Brew installs the five executables listed in the catalogue data: rgbasm, rgbfix, rgbgfx, rgblink, rgbobj.
brief.standout: The toolchain is split into small single-purpose programs that the project explicitly says can be replaced or used on their own, and RGBGFX handles the art conversion step that most toy assemblers leave to you. The project also keeps its manual generated from man pages in the repository, which is unusual for a hobby toolchain.
brief.status: Active-looking but unconfirmed. The README and homepage link to a full manual, a version history, and a contribution guide, and the project is maintained through the GBDev community. I did not see a last release date or last commit date in the pages I read, so I cannot give a firm date.
brief.caveats: The README describes building from source, and the homepage points to platform-specific install pages I did not read. The scope is Game Boy and Game Boy Color only. The homepage talks about writing native assembly, so this is a low-level, assembly-first workflow. The brew caveats field is empty.

judge.reason: A focused toolchain for making real Game Boy ROMs, including converting artwork into console-native tile data, offers a hands-on doorway into constrained hardware.

entry.title: RGBDS
entry.tldr: An assembler and linker toolchain for the Game Boy and Game Boy Color: write assembly and PNG art, get a ROM that runs on the console.
entry.deeper_look:
RGBDS, the Rednex Game Boy Development System, is a set of small programs that turn assembly source and PNG images into a playable Game Boy ROM. RGBGFX converts images into the console's tile formats. RGBASM assembles source into object files. RGBLINK links those into a ROM. RGBFIX patches the ROM header and checksum so the hardware will accept it. The brew formula also installs rgbobj.

The project's own pitch is control: "Gain complete control over the console; with no middle-man, debugging is made simpler." There is no engine or runtime in between. You write native assembly for the console's CPU and decide what happens on every cycle and in every byte of memory.

The idea underneath is that a whole computer can be small enough to hold in your head. The Game Boy has tight limits on memory, graphics and sound, and fitting a game inside them teaches how assemblers, linkers, object files and ROM headers fit together. Each stage is a separate program, and the project says each can be replaced with a custom one or used standalone in another process.

The project dates back to 1997 and is maintained through the GBDev homebrew community. The homepage links to a full manual and a version history. The brief does not describe the assembly syntax in detail, so the documentation is the place to start.

entry.whats_unique: The toolchain is split into small single-purpose programs that can be swapped out or used on their own. It also includes RGBGFX, which handles the art conversion step that many hobby assemblers leave to you.
entry.caveats: It is assembly-first and covers only the Game Boy and Game Boy Color, so expect to learn the hardware as well as the tools.
